It is becoming f*cking dangerous

Anthropic just dropped one of the best tricks for Claude Code

The concept: run Sonnet, Haiku, and Opus 5.5 simultaneously, with each model handling only what it does best

Get Opus-level decision-making on every critical choice without paying Opus prices for routine operations

Simply launch Claude Code like this: claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

Here is the breakdown of responsibilities:

> Sonnet 5.5 runs the active session and writes the code
> Haiku 5.5 explores files and documentation in parallel
> Opus 5.5 stays on standby as an advisor for major decisions
> You stop wasting Opus budgets on tasks that don't require it

Opus only steps in during three specific scenarios:

> Before locking in a plan
> When the exact same error happens twice
> Before declaring the task complete

Sonnet builds. Haiku explores. Opus reviews

JEV engineering applies the exact same logic one layer down: micro-decisions that require no deep reasoning (choosing files, selecting tools, deciding to retry or stop) are processed by JEV in milliseconds, leaving the large models to handle only the actual splits

The complete tree structure:

Sonnet 5.5 runs the primary session and edits code search maps the repository using Haiku 5.5 grep finds call sites using Haiku 5.5 docs pulls API references using Haiku 5.5 Opus 5.5 acts as an on-call advisor, reading the full transcript when consulted JEV routes micro-forks within milliseconds

Paste this tree and prompt directly into Claude Code: 

Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:

1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 acting as an advisor
2. Create three read-only Haiku 5.5 subagents: search (maps the repository) grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls API references)
3. Add a single rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before locking a plan, after encountering the same error twice, and before marking a task as done
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool selection, path routing, retries) through JEV. Show every change as a diff first. Do not apply edits until I give the go-ahead

Save this, you will use it every single day
